newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mubarak says Mideast freeze could foster terrorism.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak says Mideast freeze could foster terrorism.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak cautioned in an interview published on Monday that stalling the Middle East peace process may foster terrorism rather than war.
Mubarak told the French daily Le Figaro that he did not think war, between Syria and Israel for example, was likely.
"But violence, yes, and that is much more complicated to manage than war...How do you control terrorism? Is it the (Moslem) fundamentalists who benefit from tension?" he asked.

"(Those who benefit) are all those who are against peace, and there are many of them: in Israel as in other countries, there are some in Egypt too. There are many in Iran too who refuse the victory of peace," Mubarak said.

The Egyptian president urged Israel to drop its demand that its troops be allowed to enter PLO-run areas in the West Bank town of Hebron -- where 400 Jews live amidst 100,000 Arabs -- in "hot pursuit" of suspected guerrillas.

"(The hot pursuit demand) is equivalent to creating an authority above the Palestinian authority. That will not be accepted, not even by Palestinian citizens. It will lead to new violence, acts of revenge," Mubarak said.

Asked whether he had lost confidence in Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Mubarak answered: "I cannot say that. I know there are difficulties. That's why I try to encourage him to act, to explain to his public opinion what has to be done for peace and stability."
"What should he do? First of all, he should realise that this right of pursuit that he demands is unacceptable for Palestinians. That is the toughest issue now," Mubarak said.
Israeli and Palestinian negotiators ended their sixth week of talks on the fate of Hebron on Friday without clinching a deal.
